plausibility_notes: Hugh faces financial ruin and a career-ending accusation; Monet needs a gift to conceal misused funds but faces an audit under Grant's conditions. Both gain substantial motives without demonstrated opportunity.
Brie has a dispute plus direct service opportunity. Chip retains knowledge of the poison and a falsified conservation record but no theft link.
Artie's undisclosed new job reduces the simple removal motive, though resentment over Grant taking credit remains. It explains rather than excludes innocence.

Every attendee admits an ethical compromise and a Grant conflict in very similarly structured statements. This distributes motive almost universally and makes narrative pattern more salient than evidence.
